# netting-set: Netting set (from CSV)

*Generated by `tools/mrloader/kind_docs.py` from the kind's contract, its mapping file and its sample: do not edit; change the mapping or the contract and run it again.*

## 1. What it is and who reads it

The netting sets, one row each: the counterparty, the legal entity, the agreement and CSA, and whether netting is enforceable. Terms and links only.

Trades that net on close-out under one agreement and CSA, with exposure and collateral.

- **Contract:** `modules/banking/packs/counterparty-risk/contracts/netting-set.contract.yaml` (pack `counterparty-risk`, class `fundamental`), key `NETTING_SET_ID`.
- **Mapping:** `tools/mrloader/kinds/netting-set.yaml` (source `canonical`); wave 2 of the CSV loaders.
- **Grain:** One row per netting set per business date, keyed by NETTING_SET_ID.

## 2. The command

```bash
python3 tools/mrloader/csv_load.py --kind netting-set --csv FILE --date YYYY-MM-DD --dry-run   # check; write nothing
python3 tools/mrloader/csv_load.py --kind netting-set --csv FILE --date YYYY-MM-DD --inbox     # convert and hand to the data inbox
python3 tools/mrloader/csv_load.py --kind netting-set --template                                       # the header and an example row
```

In a day file: `netting-set: {csv: "FILE"}`. A bank's own column names: a mapping file of its own, given with `--mapping FILE`.

## 3. The CSV, column by column

The file's format: delimiter `,`, encoding `utf-8`, decimal `.`, thousands `,`, dates `YYYY-MM-DD` (declared in the mapping's `csv:` block over `kinds/shared/csv.yaml`; never guessed). Column names compare upper-cased, other characters as `_`.

| Column | Required | Field | Rule | Description | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NETTING_SET_ID` | yes | `NETTING_SET_ID` | upper-cased, other characters `-`; prefixed `NS-` unless it has it; text, kept as written | The record's id (the business key) |  |
| `COUNTERPARTY` | yes | `COUNTERPARTY` | upper-cased, other characters `-`; prefixed `CP-` unless it has it; text, kept as written | The counterparty of the netting set: a COUNTERPARTY_ID of the core pack's counterparty kind (CP-…). |  |
| `AGREEMENT` | yes | `AGREEMENT` | upper-cased, other characters `-`; prefixed `AGR-` unless it has it; text, kept as written | The master agreement whose close-out netting defines the set: an AGREEMENT_ID of the agreement kind (AGR-…). |  |
| `CSA` | no | `CSA` | upper-cased, other characters `-`; prefixed `CSA-` unless it has it; text, kept as written | The CSA margining the set: a CSA_ID of the csa kind (CSA-…), one per agreement and bank legal entity (decision 9); absent for an unmargined set. | empty: an unmargined set |
| `CREDIT_LIMIT` | no | `CREDIT_LIMIT` | upper-cased, other characters `-`; prefixed `LIM-` unless it has it; text, kept as written | The counterparty's credit limit: a LIMIT_ID of the credit-limit kind (LIM-…). |  |
| `COLLATERAL_BALANCE` | no | `COLLATERAL_BALANCE` | upper-cased, other characters `-`; prefixed `COLL-` unless it has it; text, kept as written | The set's collateral balance: a BALANCE_ID of the collateral-balance kind (COLL-…). |  |
| `LEGAL_ENTITY` | yes | `LEGAL_ENTITY` | upper-cased, other characters `-`; prefixed `LE-` unless it has it; text, kept as written | The bank's legal entity on the bank's side of the set: an ENTITY_ID of the core pack's legal-entity kind (LE-…). |  |
| `NETTING_ENFORCEABLE` | yes | `NETTING_ENFORCEABLE` | true/false, Y/N, 1/0 | true when a legal opinion confirms close-out netting is enforceable for the set; false treats the trades gross. | true when close-out netting holds in law |

## 5. What is not loaded

| Name | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `TRADE_COUNT` | a column of this name | the set's trades are the valuations that name it |
| `NET_MTM` | a column of this name | computed from the set's trade valuations |
| `COLLATERAL` | a column of this name | computed from the set's collateral balance |
| `CVA` | a column of this name | computed by the CVA engine |
| `TRADE_COUNT` | derived | a roll-up Drishti computes from the set's trade valuations; a master file does not carry it and an upstream value is ignored |
| `NET_MTM` | derived | a roll-up Drishti computes from the set's trade valuations; a master file does not carry it and an upstream value is ignored |
| `COLLATERAL` | derived | a roll-up Drishti computes from the set's collateral balance; a master file does not carry it and an upstream value is ignored |
| `LIMIT` | derived | a roll-up Drishti computes from the counterparty's credit limit; a master file does not carry it and an upstream value is ignored |
| `CVA` | derived | a roll-up Drishti computes from the CVA engine's result; a master file does not carry it and an upstream value is ignored |
| `TRADES` | derived | a roll-up Drishti computes from the set's trade valuations; a master file does not carry it and an upstream value is ignored |
| `BY_ASSET` | derived | a roll-up Drishti computes from the set's trade valuations; a master file does not carry it and an upstream value is ignored |

## 6. Checks

- **A rejected row:** `on-reject: refuse` (any rejected row refuses the whole kind: fix the file and run again). A duplicate key always refuses it.
- **Unique:** `NETTING_SET_ID` per business date.
- **Link** `COUNTERPARTY` to `counterparty`: policy `refuse` (mr_run.py checks it against the day's `counterparty` file, else `--against`; a target found nowhere is *not checked*).
- **Link** `AGREEMENT` to `agreement`: policy `warn` (mr_run.py checks it against the day's `agreement` file, else `--against`; a target found nowhere is *not checked*).
- **Link** `CSA` to `csa`: policy `refuse` (mr_run.py checks it against the day's `csa` file, else `--against`; a target found nowhere is *not checked*).
- **Link** `CREDIT_LIMIT` to `credit-limit`: policy `warn` (mr_run.py checks it against the day's `credit-limit` file, else `--against`; a target found nowhere is *not checked*).
- **Link** `COLLATERAL_BALANCE` to `collateral-balance`: policy `warn` (mr_run.py checks it against the day's `collateral-balance` file, else `--against`; a target found nowhere is *not checked*).
- **Link** `LEGAL_ENTITY` to `legal-entity`: policy `warn` (mr_run.py checks it against the day's `legal-entity` file, else `--against`; a target found nowhere is *not checked*).
- **Link** `TRADES[].BOOK` to `book`: policy `warn` (mr_run.py checks it against the day's `book` file, else `--against`; a target found nowhere is *not checked*).

Reject codes it can give: `MISSING_REQUIRED`, `BAD_BOOLEAN`, `EXCEL_NUMBER_ID`, `BAD_ENUM`, `BAD_PATTERN`, `DUPLICATE_KEY`, `EXCEL_ERROR`, `FORMULA`, `BAD_ROW_SHAPE`.
Each line of `<kind>.<date>.rejects.csv` gives FILE, ROW (as a spreadsheet shows it), KEY, COLUMN, FIELD, VALUE, REASON, WHY, FIX.

## 7. Before and after

- **Load first:** `csa`, `counterparty`, `legal-entity`.
- **Then:** `collateral-balance`, `trade-valuation`.

## 8. Repeat, restate, remove

- **Again for the same date:** the same command; the date's `netting-set` rows are replaced as a whole (`mode: replace`).
- **Restate a past date:** run with that `--date`; to change one row, send the whole file again.
- **Remove the date:** `python3 tools/drishti.py lake delete --lake LAKE --kind netting-set --date YYYY-MM-DD --dry-run` (then without `--dry-run`).
